# Round 3 plan: triage

I read the round 2 prediction log, failures F4 to F6, the four proposals, and `spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml`. Round 2 went badly for the predictions. The naive guess ("same as last round") was closer in 4 of 5 rows, and the only hit was a tie. The stop streak is 0. This round stays close to the round 2 measured numbers and moves a number only where a change has a stated cause.

Two details were missing, so I picked defaults. Round 2's last requirement ID is unknown, so this round starts at R20. The pasted log gives priority only for C, so A and B priority start at 0.78. Before I save the YAML, I will replace 0.78 with the regraded r02 values for A and B, and I will keep the prediction equal to the baseline.

## 1. Specify

### Proposals from round 2

| ID | Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Split the outage status check out of C's merged tool | Adopt as a new config E. C stays unchanged. | Changing C in place would make C differ from round 2 in one way and from B in two ways. A new E = C plus one separate tool measures the F4 fix against C in the same round. |
| P2 | Add 10 harder tickets (mixed billing and outage) | Reject for round 3 (default) | 0.86 is not a ceiling. The ceiling rule needs every config at the maximum of 1.0. The 10 tickets also have no reference labels from the support lead, and the author must not write the labels the grader uses. Logged as D7. |
| P3 | Drop config D | Adopt | D scored 0.74 on category and cost $0.004 per ticket against a $0.002 prediction. F6 has no fix yet. Running D again would spend budget to see F6 again. F6 stays open. |
| P4 | Raise trials per cell from 3 to 5 | Adopt | B missed by 0.02, which is inside trial noise at n=3. n=5 narrows the per-cell spread. |

### Requirements (round 3)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R20 | Config E is C with the outage status check as its own tool, which makes 4 tools. The prompt, model, and other tools match C exactly. | P1, r02 F4 | Harness config diff check: E differs from C only in the tool list, and that list has 4 entries including `outage_status`. |
| R21 | On every outage-labeled ticket, E calls `outage_status` before it sets a priority. | r02 F4 | Transcript code check `status_called_before_priority` on the outage slice. |
| R22 | When the status check reports an active incident, the agent assigns P1 or P2 to the outage ticket. | r02 F4 | `grade.py` priority check on the outage slice against `label.priority`. |
| R23 | `grade.py` reads priority only from `label.priority`. It never reads priority from the draft reply. | r02 F5 | Selftest case: the draft says "P3" and the label says P1. The grader must score the label. |
| R24 | Each cell runs 5 trials. A split cell gets up to 3 extra trials. | P4 | Harness trial count check and the completeness critic. |
| R25 | Config D is retired for round 3. F6 stays open. | P3, r02 F6 | The config list has no D. The log notes the retirement. |
| R26 | C runs unchanged as the F4 control. | P1 decision | Config hash for C matches round 2. |
| R27 | Spend stays under the round cap. Any trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged. | Budget | Harness cap check and skip log. |

### Disagreements (new rows)

| ID | Question | Option A | Option B | Work affected | Decides | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D7 | Add harder tickets? | Add 10 once the support lead labels them | Keep the 40 tickets | Task set, baselines | User and support lead | Default B for r03. Revisit when labels exist. |
| D8 | Where does the F4 fix go? | Change C in place | Add E and keep C | Config list | User | Default B (one change per config). |
| D9 | What happens to Haiku? | Drop D | Keep D and cap retries | Cost metric | User | Default A until F6 has a fix. |

## 2. Predict

All configs run on Sonnet 5.5, with the same 40 tickets and n=5. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band.

### Category accuracy (grader check: `grade.py` exact match of `label.category` against the reference)

| Config | Same as last round | Predicted | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0.86 | 0.86 ± 0.04 | Nothing changed. |
| B | 0.86 | 0.86 ± 0.04 | Round 2 showed no gain from the shorter prompt. My +0.02 Why missed. |
| C | 0.80 | 0.80 ± 0.04 | C is unchanged because it is the control. |
| E | (new, parent C 0.80) | 0.85 ± 0.04 | With status evidence back, outage tickets stop drifting to "bug". It stays at or below B because the other merges remain. |

### Priority accuracy (grader check: `grade.py` on `label.priority`, after the F5 fix)

| Config | Same as last round | Predicted | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0.78 (assumed) | 0.78 ± 0.05 | Nothing changed. |
| B | 0.78 (assumed) | 0.78 ± 0.05 | Nothing changed. |
| C | 0.71 | 0.71 ± 0.05 | F4 is still present in C. |
| E | (new, parent C 0.71) | 0.78 ± 0.05 | Outage tickets get P1 or P2 again once the status check is visible. |

### Outage status check call rate on outage-labeled tickets (grader check: transcript code check `status_called_before_priority`)

| Config | Same as last round | Predicted | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | not measured | 0.90 ± 0.08 | The status tool is separate in A. |
| B | not measured | 0.90 ± 0.08 | Same tools as A. |
| C | 0.00 (F4) | 0.00 ± 0.05 | F4 says C never called the check. |
| E | (new) | 0.90 ± 0.08 | Same tool exposure as A for this one check. |

### Cost per ticket (grader check: API usage tokens times the pinned price table)

| Config | Same as last round | Predicted | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A, B, C | r02 measured | r02 value ± 15% | Nothing changed. |
| E | (new) | 1.05 × C ± 0.10 | One extra tool definition plus the status calls on outage tickets. |

## 3. Evaluate

### Gates, in order. A failed gate halts the run and I report back.

1. **Grader selftest.** Oracle labels must score 1.0. Empty output and wrong labels must fail. The F5 case from R23 must score the label.
2. **Control regrade.** I regrade the r02 transcripts with the current `grade.py`. The result must match the regraded r02 numbers exactly: category A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, and priority C 0.71.
3. **Dry run on 3 cells.** The cells are C on T17, E on T17, and A on one billing ticket. I check the trial schema, the status-call detector, cost logging, and the peek scan.

### Workflow arguments

- `ROUND = 3`, held in one constant. No round number is typed into any prompt text.
- Configs: A, B, C, E. Tickets: the same 40 as r02. Trials: 5 per cell. Split cells get up to 3 extra trials.
- Trial schema: `category`, `priority`, `draft_reply`, `tool_calls`, `usage`.
- Code checks run first. No judge runs this round because draft reply quality is not a metric.
- Trials cannot read `grade.py`, the reference labels, or `spe/predictions/`. I scan every transcript for reads of those paths and void any trial that touched them.
- The run ends with failure analysis and a completeness critic.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The base run is 4 configs × 40 tickets × 5 trials, which is 800 trials. Split-cell extras add at most 4 × 40 × 3 more, but in practice they should add about 100. At a rough $0.012 per Sonnet ticket, the run costs about $11. I will replace the $0.012 with the r02 measured costs before launch. The hard cap is $20.

## After approval

1. Save your prompt "ok, next one" and any plan corrections, word for word, to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Add the round 3 table to `spe/spec/spec.md` and D7 to D9 to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit as `spe(r03): specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with the header `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`, round 3, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs A/B/C/E, each number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round`. Commit as `spe(r03): predict`.
3. Run gates 1 to 3, then launch the Workflow and commit the harness as `spe(r03): evaluate`.
4. When the completion notice arrives, close out the round and commit and tag it as `spe(r03): learn`.

Nothing is pushed.
critiques: The answer is titled "Round 3 plan: triage". It reads the round 2 log, failures, and proposals, then opens with a Specify phase that handles the proposals as a respec. It did this without being told the phase.

The proposals table gives each of P1 to P4 a decision and a reason. P1 is adopted as new config E so C stays a control. P2 is rejected because 0.86 is not a ceiling and the new tickets have no labels. P3 is adopted because of F6 and the cost miss. P4 is adopted because B's miss is inside noise.
The Source column cites the failure IDs. R20 to R22 cite "r02 F4", R23 cites "r02 F5", and R25 cites "r02 F6".

Category predictions start from the draft baselines (A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80), and every number has a ± band. A and B priority use an assumed 0.78, but the answer flags this and commits to swapping in the regraded r02 values before saving. Cost is given as "r02 value ± 15%".
Every prediction row has a Why. Examples are "Nothing changed.", "C is unchanged because it is the control.", and for E, "Outage tickets get P1 or P2 again once the status check is visible."

After-approval step 2 writes spe/predictions/r03.yaml with a do-not-edit header and commits it as "spe(r03): predict". Step 3 then runs the gates and launches the eval, so no trial runs before the prediction is committed.

The Evaluate section lists ordered gates that halt the run on failure. They are a grader selftest, a control regrade of the r02 transcripts that must match the regraded numbers, and a 3-cell dry run. All three come before the full run.
